newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle exits local haul business.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle exits local haul business.

text.p: American Eagle Group Inc said on Monday it was withdrawing from the local and intermediate-haul trucking business due to poor performance and increased price competition.
The company also said in a statement it would discontinue its quarterly dividend, effective with the dividend scheduled to be paid in October.

"American Eagle has recently had several challenging quarters," Chairman and Chief Executive M. Philip Guthrie said in a statement. "We have reviewed each of our operating segments and taken aggressive actions to improve the operating results of segments not performing up to our expectation."
He said the decision to exit the local and intermediate-haul trucking line would allow the company to focus on core businesses. This division would also have significant staff reductions, he said.
"During 1996 the company's trucking line of busines has been its primary source of unacceptable underwriting results," the insurance holding company said.
American Eagle was not immediately available to comment on if it would take a charge for the withdrawal or the staff reductions. It said it also cut staff at its aviation unit.
The company said it decided to cut the dividend to increase its capital quickly.
Regarding raising more capital, it said: "We are currently evaluating various alternatives and structures and plan to have a transaction announced in the near future."
American Eagle also said President and Chief Operating Officer George Cass retired and Guthrie would assume the position of president.
Cass would continue to serve as a consultant to the company, it said.
